claims.text: The target material class comprises high-entropy alloys with varying compositions and processing conditions.
Machine-learning algorithms should be incorporated into the melting-property prediction workflow.
The machine-learning algorithms should be trained using high-entropy-alloy composition data.
The machine-learning algorithms should be trained using processing-condition data.
The machine-learning algorithms should be trained using measured melting-property data.
Machine-learning models can identify complex relationships between composition, processing conditions, and melting properties.
Learning these relationships will improve the accuracy of melting-property predictions.
The proposed approach will predict melting temperature more accurately than current traditional methods.
The proposed approach will improve predictions of melting properties other than melting temperature.
The proposed approach will be more computationally efficient than current traditional prediction methods.
The hypothesis is limited to high-entropy alloys for which composition, processing-condition, and melting-property data are available.
Prediction accuracy depends on the quality and quantity of training data.
Prediction accuracy depends on the choice of machine-learning algorithm.
Performance should be evaluated against traditional methods on a hold-out dataset of high-entropy alloys using mean absolute error and root mean squared error.
The hypothesis is falsified if the machine-learning method does not outperform traditional methods in both mean absolute error and root mean squared error.
